<USER_REQUEST>
/automation Guide me through creating an automated task
PROMPT 1: Compare and merge the two apps

I'm building a tractor repair product for the first time. It is in the build/testing phase and nothing is published. I have two separate apps (customer and mechanic) and an admin web dashboard. I'm merging the customer and mechanic apps into ONE app. Do not touch the admin dashboard yet.

1. Compare both apps: completed screens, code quality, navigation, state management, backend integration, bugs. Tell me which is the better base and why. Wait for my confirmation before merging.

2. After I confirm, move the other app's screens, components, services and navigation into the base app as separate stacks (customer stack and mechanic stack). Resolve duplicate files and name conflicts carefully. Do not rewrite working code.

3. The app name is not decided. Do not invent one. Put the name in a single config constant with the placeholder "AppName".

4. Merge dependencies, permissions (location, camera, microphone, notifications), and .env variables into one config. Use one package name and one icon.

5. REAL DATA ONLY. Find and list every mock array, hardcoded JSON, Math.random(), placeholder name/phone/rating, setTimeout-faked response, and any button labelled "Prototype: ...". Remove them. Replace with the real database, real phone OTP, and Google Places only for nearby shops. Never fall back to fake data. If the database has old test records, list them and delete only after I confirm.

6. After the merge works, delete leftover mock files and the unused app folder code.

7. Run the app and show me what works and what breaks.

Rules: If a decision is unclear or you need an API key or access, stop and ask me. Do not guess or fake.

PROMPT 2: Build the full flow from the UI design(pdf is in reference folder tractor repairapp(protopype)
The UI design in /design is the source of truth for screens and layout. It is a prototype: text in [square brackets] marks fields that must come from the real database, and any button labelled "Prototype: ..." must NOT be built. Do not rewrite working code. Real data only.

APP STRUCTURE (one app, two roles)
1. Flow: language screen (English / Telugu / Hindi, saved, changeable in Settings) → role selection ("I need a mechanic" / "I'm a mechanic") → phone OTP sign in for both roles. Use the OTP length the auth provider supports (6 digits) and update the code boxes to match. The role is fixed after sign up.
2. Mechanic registration as in the design. New mechanics stay "pending" until approved in the admin dashboard.

CUSTOMER FLOW
3. New repair request: saved tractors (add/edit), problem area, voice note recording, photo/video (compressed), GPS pin with "Move pin".
4. Dispatch: a server-side function offers the request to the nearest approved, online mechanic who handles that problem area, one at a time, with 30 seconds to accept. On decline or timeout, offer to the next nearest. After a configurable max number of mechanics or minutes, show a "No mechanic available" screen with Retry and Cancel.
5. Mechanic assigned: real mechanic details, distance, live ETA only if real location sharing works (otherwise no ETA), start code generated server-side, Call button, Cancel.
6. Quote screen: Approve or Decline.
   - If the customer approves, work continues.
   - If the customer declines AFTER the mechanic has arrived (start code entered), the customer owes only the visit charge. The mechanic marks "Visit charge collected (cash)", the job closes as "quote_declined", and the visit charge is recorded.
   - If the customer cancels before the mechanic arrives, there is NO fee. Record the cancellation and its reason, and increase the customer's cancellation count.
   - If the mechanic cancels or never arrives, the customer pays nothing and the mechanic's cancellation count increases.
7. Bill screen: visit charge, approved quote, spare parts, total, finish code, pay cash or online. Amounts are calculated on the server.
8. Rating after a completed job only, plus "Report a problem" saved for admin review. Add a Contact support screen.
9. Customer home with request history and saved tractors.

MECHANIC FLOW
10. Home: online/offline toggle (location shared only while online), today's earnings, jobs, rating, platform fee balance, all computed from real jobs.
11. New request screen: 30-second countdown enforced by the server, distance, map pin, problem, photo, voice note. Customer mobile number stays hidden until Accept.
12. Active job: Call, Navigate (opens Google Maps), start code entry (validated server-side), send quote, Start repair.
13. Collect payment: enter spare parts amount, total auto-calculated, finish code from customer, "Cash received · mark job done".
14. Job history and earnings screen.

STATUS FLOW (enforced server-side, no skipping)
requested → offered → accepted → started (start code) → quote_sent → quote_approved → in_progress → bill_ready → paid → completed. Also: cancelled, declined, no_mechanic_found, quote_declined.

PAYMENTS
15. Phase 1: cash only. Store visit charge, quote, parts, total and platform fee for every job.
   - Read these from an app_settings table, never hardcode them: platform_fee_percent (default 10), visit_charge_amount (default 200).
   - The platform fee is calculated on the server as a percentage of the total bill and added to the mechanic's fee balance on cash jobs.
   - If a job closes as "quote_declined", the visit charge is the total, and the platform fee is calculated on it the same way.
   - Seed these two default values in app_settings. They are configuration, not mock data.
16. Online payment (UPI/card) and "Pay now" for the fee balance: build the UI behind a feature flag, connected to Razorpay TEST mode only after I give you keys. Never mark anything paid without server-side verification.

SECURITY
17. Row Level Security: customers see only their own requests. Mechanics see only offers sent to them and jobs they accepted. Codes and amounts are generated and calculated on the server, never trusted from the app. Photos, videos and voice notes go in private storage. Test the policies and show me the results.

NOTIFICATIONS, LANGUAGE, NETWORK
18. Push notifications (FCM): new offer, accepted, quote sent, quote approved, quote declined, bill ready, completed.
19. All text in i18n files for English, Telugu, Hindi. The speaker icon reads the screen aloud using device text-to-speech.
20. Weak network: retry uploads, save the request draft, clear errors, never show success unless the server confirmed it.

REAL DATA ONLY
21. No mock mechanics, requests or statuses. Loading, error and empty states everywhere. Keys in .env.

Rules: If a decision is unclear or you need a key, stop and ask me. Do not guess or fake.

PROMPT 3: Admin dashboard
Update the existing admin web dashboard to work with the merged app's database. Do not rewrite working code. Real data only.

1. Admin login with real auth. Only users with an admin role can open it. No shared or hardcoded passwords.
2. Mechanic approvals: list pending mechanics with name, phone, skills, photo and ID document (private storage, viewed through short-lived signed links). Approve, reject (with reason), or suspend. Changing status updates the database and notifies the mechanic.
3. All repair requests: filter by status, date, problem area, mechanic. Open any request to see its full status history, quote, bill and ratings.
4. Reported problems: list customer reports with the related job, mark as open / resolved, and add admin notes.
5. Mechanic fee balances: show the platform fee owed per mechanic from cash jobs, with a way to record a payment received.
6. Block or unblock any customer or mechanic. Blocked users cannot sign in or receive offers.
7. Summary cards (total jobs, active jobs, approved mechanics, pending approvals) computed from real data only.
8. Enforce admin-only access with Row Level Security and server-side checks, not just hidden buttons. Test and show me the results.
9. Loading, error and empty states. Keys in .env.
10. Settings page (admin only): view and edit platform_fee_percent and visit_charge_amount from app_settings. Every change records who changed it and when. Changes apply only to new jobs, never to completed ones. Also show cancellation counts per customer and mechanic, and let me block users with repeated cancellations.

Rules: No mock data. If a decision is unclear or you need access, stop and ask me.

PROMPT 4: Two-phone testing setup

TWO-PHONE TESTING SETUP

1. Detect the framework (Expo, React Native, or Flutter) and build an installable Android APK that works on any phone without a laptop (not Expo Go, not a debug build tied to my computer). Save it in a clear folder and tell me the exact file path.

2. Show a version number inside the app (Settings or login screen) so I know which build each phone has.

3. Give me exact steps to install this APK on 2 different Android phones: via USB with `adb install`, or by sharing the file through Google Drive. Also give the steps to upload it to Firebase App Distribution so both testers get an install link.

4. Create test accounts: one customer and one mechanic with different phone numbers. Use Supabase or Firebase test phone numbers with fixed OTP codes for the build phase only, and mark them clearly as test accounts. Approve the test mechanic in the admin dashboard.

5. Give me a step-by-step test checklist for the two phones:
   - Phone 1 (customer): choose language and role, sign up, create a repair request with photo, voice note and location.
   - Phone 2 (mechanic): receive the push notification, see the request, accept within 30 seconds.
   - Test decline and timeout so the request goes to the next mechanic, and the "No mechanic available" screen.
   - Start code, send quote, approve quote, finish code, cash payment, mark done.
   - Quote declined after arrival: customer pays only the visit charge, job closes as quote_declined.
   - Customer cancels before arrival (no fee, cancellation count goes up) and mechanic cancels.
   - Check that platform fee and visit charge match the values in app_settings, and that changing them in the admin Settings page applies only to new jobs.
   - Rating, Report a problem, Call buttons.
   - Weak network (airplane mode on and off mid-upload).

6. Add logging so any failure can be traced, and tell me how to view the logs (`adb logcat` or the debug console).

Rules: You cannot install on my phones yourself. Give me the APK and exact steps. If a decision is unclear or you need access, stop and ask me.
</USER_REQUEST>

1: ---
2: name: automation
3: description: Interactive guide to design and create a scheduled background automation. Use this skill when the user wants to create an automated or recurring scheduled task (e.g. "summarize my emails every morning", "every Monday send me a to-do list"). Also triggered by the /automation slash command.
4: metadata:
5:   icon: schedule
6: ---
7: 
8: # Scheduled Automations
9: 
10: A **scheduled automation** is a background sidecar (`"builtin": "schedule"`)
11: that runs on a cron schedule and starts a fresh agent conversation (`agentapi
12: new-conversation`) on each run.
13: 
14: This skill is **strictly for scheduled (cron) automations**. Do not use it to
15: create UI sidecars, continuous generic command/daemon sidecars, or in-turn
16: timers (use the `schedule` tool instead).
17: 
18: ## Quick Start (5-Turn Creation Flow)
19: 
20: 1.  **Turn 1 — Cadence**: Ask via `ask_question` (`Hourly`, `Daily`, `Weekly`,
21:     or `Custom cron schedule`).
22: 2.  **Turn 2 — Time / Day**: Ask for the specific time or day of week
23:     (`ask_question`).
24: 3.  **Turn 3 — Task Prompt**: Ask what the agent should do on each run and
25:     refine into a self-contained prompt.
26: 4.  **Turn 4 — Write `sidecar.json`**: Create
27:     `~/.gemini/jetski/sidecars/<slug>/sidecar.json` with `"builtin":
28:     "schedule"`, `"args": {"schedule": "<cron>", "prompt": "<prompt>"}`.
29: 5.  **Turn 5 — Optional Test Run**: Offer to test the prompt immediately via
30:     `agentapi new-conversation`.
31: 
32: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
33: 
34: ## Interactive Creation Workflow
35: 
36: Guide the user through creating the automation **one step at a time** across
37: turns. If the user already provided some details in their initial prompt (such
38: as the schedule or the task), skip the questions already answered and proceed to
39: the next missing step.
40: 
41: ### Turn 1: Ask for the Cadence
42: 
43: If the schedule cadence is not yet specified, use the `ask_question` tool to
44: ask:
45: 
46: -   **Question**: `"What should be the cadence of the automation?"`
47: -   **Options**:
48:     -   `Hourly`
49:     -   `Daily`
50:     -   `Weekly`
51:     -   `Custom cron schedule`
52: 
53: Wait for the user's response before moving to the next question.
54: 
55: ### Turn 2: Confirm the Specific Time / Day
56: 
57: Based on the chosen cadence, confirm the exact schedule in a follow-up turn
58: using `ask_question`:
59: 
60: -   **If Daily**: Use `ask_question` to confirm the hour of the day (e.g., `9:00
61:     AM`, `12:00 PM`, `5:00 PM`; the user can also enter a custom time via the
62:     built-in write-in option).
63: -   **If Weekly**: Use `ask_question` to confirm both the day(s) of the week
64:     (e.g., `Monday`, `Friday`, `Weekdays (Mon–Fri)`) and the hour of the day
65:     (e.g., `9:00 AM`, `5:00 PM`).
66: -   **If Hourly**: Default to the top of every hour (`0 * * * *`), or confirm if
67:     they want a specific minute offset.
68: -   **If Custom cron schedule**: Ask the user to specify their desired cron
69:     expression or interval (e.g., `*/30 * * * *` for every 30 minutes).
70: 
71: Wait for the user's response before asking what the task should do.
72: 
73: ### Turn 3: Ask What the Task Should Do
74: 
75: Once the schedule is set (and if the task itself has not been described yet),
76: ask the user in plain text (do **not** use `ask_question` for this open-ended
77: step):
78: 
79: > *"What would you like the task to do? (For example: 'Summarize my unread
80: > emails from the last 24 hours and highlight any that need a reply' or 'Check
81: > my open pull requests and list any with failing checks.')"*
82: 
83: Wait for the user's response.
84: 
85: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
86: 
87: ## Step 4: Create `sidecar.json` & Offer a Test Run to Configure Permissions
88: 
89: ### 1. Translate Schedule & Author Self-Contained Run Prompt
90: 
91: -   **Cron schedule**: Standard 5-field cron expression (`minute hour
92:     day-of-month month day-of-week`) written in the user's local time, always
93:     prefixed with `CRON_TZ=<IANA zone> ` so it runs in the user's timezone:
94:     -   Hourly: `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 * * * *`
95:     -   Daily at 9:00 AM: `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 * * *`
96:     -   Daily at 5:00 PM: `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 17 * * *`
97:     -   Weekly on Monday at 9:00 AM: `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 * * 1`
98:     -   Weekdays at 9:00 AM: `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 * * 1-5`
99: -   **Determine the user's timezone** (an IANA name such as `Europe/Zurich`;
100:     never an abbreviation like `PST` or a raw offset like `+02:00`):
101:     1.  If the user already stated a timezone or city, use the matching IANA
102:         zone.
103:     2.  Otherwise detect the host's timezone (map any OS-specific zone name to
104:         its IANA equivalent).
105:     3.  If detection fails, use `ask_question` to confirm the user's timezone
106:         (offer the detected zone plus a few common zones; the user can write in
107:         their own).
108:     4.  If the user supplies a custom cron that already starts with `CRON_TZ=`
109:         or `TZ=`, keep it as-is and do not add a second prefix.
110:     5.  When confirming the schedule to the user, state it with the zone (e.g.,
111:         "every day at 9:00 AM Europe/Zurich time").
112: -   **Self-contained prompt**: Each scheduled run starts a brand-new
113:     conversation with no memory of prior runs. Write a clear, self-contained
114:     prompt stating the data sources, actions, and desired output format.
115: 
116: ### 2. Announce Automation Creation & Write `<configDir>/sidecars/<sidecar-id>/sidecar.json`
117: 
118: Before calling `write_to_file`, **always output a short message to the user**
119: stating that you are now creating the **`<display_name>`** automation (do not
120: mention `sidecar.json` or internal file details to the user). Also set
121: `toolAction` / `toolSummary` on `write_to_file` to `"Creating <display_name>
122: automation"`.
123: 
124: Create the configuration file at:
125: 
126: ```
127: <configDir>/sidecars/<sidecar-id>/sidecar.json
128: ```
129: 
130: -   `<configDir>` is the user's `.gemini/config` directory (typically
131:     `~/.gemini/config`).
132: -   `<sidecar-id>` is a short, unique `kebab-case` identifier derived from the
133:     task (e.g., `daily-pr-check`).
134: -   Choose a clear, human-readable **`display_name`** (e.g., `"Daily PR Status
135:     Check"`). You MUST tell the user this exact `display_name` when pointing
136:     them to the Automations dashboard so they know which automation to enable.
137: -   Use **snake_case** field names only (`restart_policy`, `display_name`,
138:     `agent_permissions`, `access_grants`, `workspace_uris`).
139: -   Use lowercase string literals for **`restart_policy`** (`"always"` is
140:     required for `"builtin": "schedule"` and continuous daemons; `"on-failure"`
141:     or `"never"` apply only to one-shot `"command"` sidecars) — never proto enum
142:     names like `"SIDECAR_RESTART_POLICY_ALWAYS"` or `"unless-stopped"`.
143: -   Never place `sidecar.json` or scripts inside an ephemeral CitC workspace
144:     (`/google/src/cloud/<user>/<workspace>/...`) or point symlinks in
145:     `~/.gemini/config/` to an ephemeral CitC workspace that may later be
146:     deleted.
147: 
148: > [!CAUTION] **Never Hallucinate Tools or Permissions**: - Do **NOT** guess or
149: > invent MCP servers (`mcp(...)`) or CLI commands (`command(...)`) that you have
150: > not verified exist in the current environment. - Only include an
151: > `mcp(<server>/<tool>)` grant if `<server>` is actually present in your
152: > `<mcp_servers>` system prompt block. - Only include a `command(<prefix>)`
153: > grant if you have verified the binary/subcommand exists (e.g., via an
154: > available skill or a live test run). - Never use overly generic wildcards
155: > (`command(*)`, `read_file(*)`, `read_file(/)`, `write_file(*)`, `mcp(*)`,
156: > `read_url(*)`) or invalid wrapper syntax like `allow(*)`.
157: 
158: #### Example `sidecar.json`
159: 
160: ```json
161: {
162:   "builtin": "schedule",
163:   "args": [
164:     "CRON_TZ=America/New_York 0 9 * * *",
165:     "agentapi",
166:     "new-conversation",
167:     "--",
168:     "Check open pull requests in the repository and summarize any with failing CI checks or pending review comments."
169:   ],
170:   "restart_policy": "always",
171:   "display_name": "Daily PR Status Check",
172:   "description": "Every day at 9:00 AM (America/New_York), checks open pull requests and summarizes failing checks or review comments.",
173:   "agent_permissions": {
174:     "access_grants": [
175:       "command(gh pr list)",
176:       "command(gh pr view)"
177:     ]
178:   }
179: }
180: ```
181: 
182: -   `args[0]` **must** be the full cron schedule as a single string, including
183:     the `CRON_TZ=<zone>` prefix (never omit `args[0]` or place the executable at
184:     `args[0]` when `"builtin": "schedule"` is set).
185: -   Always use **absolute paths** for any local script arguments in `args`
186:     (never bare relative filenames like `"watcher.py"` or paths inside ephemeral
187:     workspaces that may later be deleted).
188: -   Always include `"--"` immediately before the prompt string in `args` so the
189:     prompt is cleanly separated from `agentapi new-conversation` flags.
190: 
191: ### 3. Point to the Dashboard (with Automation Name) & Ask to Test-Run for Reliable Permissions
192: 
193: > [!CAUTION] **DO NOT enable the automation yourself.** Never modify
194: > `user_config.json` to set `"enabled": true`, and never invoke any command or
195: > RPC to start or enable the sidecar.
196: 
197: After writing `sidecar.json`:
198: 
199: 1.  Tell the user that the automation **`<display_name>`** (`<sidecar-id>`) has
200:     been created, and explicitly instruct them to enable it in the
201:     **Automations** dashboard using the action button: `[Open Automations
202:     Dashboard](sidecar://dashboard)`
203: 2.  Explain to the user that **once enabled, the automation will run in a
204:     project that inherits global permissions and presets, and all other
205:     non-approved commands will be auto-denied**. To ensure that the automation
206:     can proceed successfully and unattended, you can execute a test run right
207:     now to configure the permissions properly.
208: 3.  Use `ask_question` to ask the user if they want you to execute a test run
209:     now:
210:     -   **Question**: `"Once enabled, '<display_name>' will run in a project
211:         that inherits global permissions and presets, and all other non-approved
212:         commands will be auto-denied. Would you like me to execute a test run
213:         now to configure its permissions properly so it can proceed
214:         successfully?"`
215:     -   **Options**:
216:         -   `(Recommended) Yes, execute a test run now to configure permissions`
217:         -   `No, I'll review permissions and enable '<display_name>' in the
218:             Automations dashboard`
219: 
220: --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
221: 
222: ## Step 5: If the User Chooses to Test-Run the Task Now
223: 
224: When the user agrees to a test run:
225: 
226: 1.  **Execute the task once in the current conversation**:
227:     -   Search for and read any relevant skills (`skill_search` / `view_file` on
228:         `SKILL.md`) or check available `<mcp_servers>` needed to fulfill the
229:         task.
230:     -   Run the actual commands, file reads/writes, URL fetches, or MCP tools to
231:         perform the task once.
232:     -   If the required tool/integration does not exist or needs
233:         authentication/setup, inform the user clearly so they know what is
234:         missing before enabling the automation.
235: 2.  **Update `sidecar.json` with the exact verified permissions**:
236:     -   Record every permission grant actually required during the test run,
237:         scoped as succinctly as possible in `agent_permissions`:
238:         -   **`workspace_uris`**: `["file:///absolute/path/to/dir"]` if the task
239:             needed read+write access to a workspace folder.
240:         -   **`access_grants`**:
241:         -   `command(<binary_and_subcommand>)` — e.g., `command(gh pr list)`
242:             (never `command(*)`).
243:         -   `read_file(<absolute_path>)` — e.g., `read_file(/Users/alice/notes)`
244:             (never `read_file(*)` or `read_file(/)`).
245:         -   `write_file(<absolute_path>)` — e.g.,
246:             `write_file(/Users/alice/digests)` (never `write_file(*)` or
247:             `write_file(/)`).
248:         -   `mcp(<server_name>/<tool_name>)` — e.g., `mcp(buganizer/get_bugs)`
249:             (only for real MCP tools actually called; never `mcp(*)`).
250:         -   `read_url(<domain>)` / `execute_url(<domain>)` — e.g.,
251:             `read_url(github.com)` (never `read_url(*)`).
252:     -   Also update the prompt in `args` if the test run revealed specific skill
253:         paths or CLI flags that will help future scheduled runs succeed reliably
254:         using those exact granted commands.
255: 3.  **Final confirmation with the Automation Name**:
256:     -   Summarize the verified permissions added to **`<display_name>`**
257:         (`<sidecar-id>`) and remind the user to enable **`<display_name>`** in
258:         the **Automations** dashboard: `[Open Automations
259:         Dashboard](sidecar://dashboard)`

Focus shifts to app-level code analysis, specifically comparing the screen implementations between the two applications. Initial examination of `customer-mobile` reveals routing based on authentication and language settings. Further dissection shows the language selection mechanism and a sign-in process utilizing phone OTP authentication with automatic profile creation.


Customer-facing screens appear to follow a logical request flow, starting from the dashboard and progressing through request creation, mechanic matching, quote approval, payment, and rating. Each stage has distinct UI components with associated data. The `match-mechanic` edge function triggers after the request's initial data is uploaded.


Analyzing `mechanic-mobile` reveals its structure: a routing switch, language selection, and authentication flows including phone OTP and password. Mechanic registration handles complete profile creation with skill input, document uploads, and GPS tracking. The home screen features duty toggling, metrics, job alerts and active job display; the earnings tab details revenue and fee management; history provides a searchable job log; and profile manages mechanic details. Job screens manage incoming requests with timers, audio notes, and location data, along with active job management via navigation, customer calls, and quote composition.


Examining the "finish job" screen reveals a critical function: capturing spare part details and final job confirmation with a running total. The mechanic app boasts more robust code architecture with error handling, offline support, and comprehensive data management across multiple tables. Conversely, the customer app offers a streamlined experience focusing on a simple user journey. The mechanic app utilizes more extensive state management. However, the customer app's state management appears minimal.

The mechanic app contains comprehensive features, including audio handling, location tracking, and mock fallback mechanisms for simulated operations, in contrast to the customer app's simpler implementation of unique file naming. The mechanic app contains advanced features like platform checks, and the customer app is focused on a streamlined flow. Both apps share the same core framework versions and utilize a shared workspace package for common dependencies.


The applications share the same state management library, but `mechanic-mobile`'s state stores significantly more data and manages the entire job lifecycle. Both apps connect to the same backend project using the same library, but `mechanic-mobile` has a more complex integration. A critical bug identified is that job codes are generated client-side, contradicting the rule that codes must be generated on the server.


The `mechanic-mobile` application's more comprehensive job lifecycle management and state machine offer advantages, despite the presence of mock hacks. The `customer-mobile` app's cleaner authentication flow and routing setup are also valuable but less critical for overall functionality. The complex feature set of `mechanic-mobile` is preferred, suggesting its state management benefits outweigh the cleanup needed to remove the testing hacks. The base should be `mechanic-mobile`.

thinking: Focusing on mechanic assignment and quote handling. Need to ensure real mechanic details are displayed, distance is accurate (ETA contingent on location sharing), and a server-side start code is generated. The quote screen requires "Approve" or "Decline" actions, with a visit charge assessed if declined *after* mechanic arrival and code entry.

If a customer declines the quote after the mechanic's arrival (indicated by start code entry), the job is marked as "quote_declined." The customer is charged only the visit fee, and the mechanic records this as "Visit charge collected (cash)," finalizing the job. Cancelling before the mechanic arrives means something else, not yet defined.

21: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.find_matching_mechanics(p_request_id UUID)
22: RETURNS TABLE (
23:   mechanic_id UUID,
24:   profile_id UUID,
25:   full_name TEXT,
26:   phone TEXT,
27:   avatar_url TEXT,
28:   rating_avg NUMERIC,
29:   total_jobs INTEGER,
30:   workshop_address TEXT,
31:   service_radius_km NUMERIC,
32:   distance_km NUMERIC
33: )
34: LANGUAGE plpgsql
35: SECURITY DEFINER
36: AS $$
37: DECLARE
38:   v_req RECORD;
39: BEGIN
40:   SELECT r.id, r.category_id, r.location, r.status
41:   INTO v_req
42:   FROM public.repair_requests r
43:   WHERE r.id = p_request_id;
44: 
45:   IF NOT FOUND THEN
46:     RAISE EXCEPTION 'Repair request not found: %', p_request_id;
47:   END IF;
48: 
49:   RETURN QUERY
50:   SELECT
51:     m.id AS mechanic_id,
52:     m.profile_id,
53:     p.full_name,
54:     p.phone,
55:     p.avatar_url,
56:     m.rating_avg,
57:     m.total_jobs,
58:     m.workshop_address,
59:     m.service_radius_km,
60:     ROUND((ST_Distance(m.current_location, v_req.location) / 1000.0)::numeric, 2) AS distance_km
61:   FROM public.mechanics m
62:   JOIN public.profiles p ON m.profile_id = p.id
63:   JOIN public.mechanic_skills ms ON ms.mechanic_id = m.id AND ms.category_id = v_req.category_id
64:   WHERE m.status = 'approved'
65:     AND m.is_online = true
66:     AND m.current_location IS NOT NULL
67:     AND v_req.location IS NOT NULL
68:     AND ST_DWithin(m.current_location, v_req.location, m.service_radius_km * 1000)
69:   ORDER BY ST_Distance(m.current_location, v_req.location) ASC;
70: END;
71: $$;

149:     job_id,

-- =============================================================
-- Migration: 00006_server_rules_and_status_enforcement.sql
-- Description: Server-side business logic and atomic RPCs for:
--              1. Customer & Mechanic cancellation tracking
--              2. Quote decline & visit charge collection
--              3. Server-side bill and platform fee calculations from app_settings
--              4. Strict status flow transition enforcement
-- =============================================================

-- -------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. CANCEL JOB BY CUSTOMER RPC
-- -------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cancel_job_by_customer(
  p_job_id UUID,
  p_reason TEXT DEFAULT 'Customer cancelled'
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_job RECORD;
  v_has_started BOOLEAN;
BEGIN
  SELECT j.*, sc.is_used as start_code_used
  INTO v_job
  FROM public.jobs j
  LEFT JOIN public.secure_codes sc ON sc.job_id = j.id AND sc.code_type = 'start'
  WHERE j.id = p_job_id;

  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
  END IF;

  v_has_started := COALESCE(v_job.start_code_used, false) OR v_job.status IN ('started', 'repair_in_progress', 'quote_approved', 'bill_ready', 'completed');

  -- If customer cancels before mechanic arrives (start code not entered), NO fee, increment cancellation_count
  IF NOT v_has_started THEN
    UPDATE public.customers
    SET cancellation_count = COALESCE(cancellation_count, 0) + 1
    WHERE id = v_job.customer_id;

    UPDATE public.jobs
    SET status = 'cancelled',
        cancelled_at = now(),
        cancellation_reason = p_reason,
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE id = p_job_id;

    UPDATE public.repair_requests
    SET status = 'cancelled',
        updated_at = now()
    WHERE id = v_job.request_id;

    INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
    VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'cancelled', 'Customer cancelled before arrival. Reason: ' || p_reason);

    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
      'success', true,
      'status', 'cancelled',
      'fee_owed', 0,
      'message', 'Job cancelled without fees as mechanic had not arrived'
    );
  ELSE
    -- If already arrived/started, customer must decline quote or pay visit charge
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Mechanic has already arrived. Please use Decline Quote flow instead of cancelling.';
  END IF;
END;
$$;

-- -------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. CANCEL JOB BY MECHANIC RPC
-- -------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cancel_job_by_mechanic(
  p_job_id UUID,
  p_reason TEXT DEFAULT 'Mechanic cancelled'
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_job RECORD;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO v_job FROM public.jobs WHERE id = p_job_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
  END IF;

  -- Mechanic cancels: customer pays nothing, mechanic's cancellation count increases
  UPDATE public.mechanics
  SET cancellation_count = COALESCE(cancellation_count, 0) + 1
  WHERE id = v_job.mechanic_id;

  UPDATE public.jobs
  SET status = 'cancelled',
      cancelled_at = now(),
      cancellation_reason = p_reason,
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = p_job_id;

  -- Put request back to matching or cancelled
  UPDATE public.repair_requests
  SET status = 'cancelled',
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = v_job.request_id;

  INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
  VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'cancelled', 'Mechanic cancelled. Reason: ' || p_reason);

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'success', true,
    'status', 'cancelled',
    'customer_owed', 0,
    'message', 'Mechanic cancelled. Customer pays nothing.'
  );
END;
$$;

-- -------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. RECORD VISIT CHARGE COLLECTED (QUOTE DECLINED) RPC
-- -------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.record_visit_charge_collected(
  p_job_id UUID
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_job RECORD;
  v_visit_charge NUMERIC := 200;
  v_platform_percent NUMERIC := 10;
  v_platform_fee NUMERIC;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO v_job FROM public.jobs WHERE id = p_job_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
  END IF;

  -- Read visit_charge_amount from app_settings
  SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 200) INTO v_visit_charge
  FROM public.app_settings
  WHERE key = 'visit_charge_amount';

  -- Read platform_fee_percent from app_settings
  SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 10) INTO v_platform_percent
  FROM public.app_settings
  WHERE key = 'platform_fee_percent';

  v_platform_fee := ROUND(v_visit_charge * (v_platform_percent / 100.0), 2);

  -- Upsert Invoice
  INSERT INTO public.invoices (
    job_id,
    visit_charge,
    repair_amount,
    parts_amount,
    subtotal,
    platform_fee,
    total,
    status
  ) VALUES (
    p_job_id,
    v_visit_charge,
    0,
    0,
    v_visit_charge,
    v_platform_fee,
    v_visit_charge,
    'paid'
  )
  ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE SET
    visit_charge = v_visit_charge,
    repair_amount = 0,
    parts_amount = 0,
    subtotal = v_visit_charge,
    platform_fee = v_platform_fee,
    total = v_visit_charge,
    status = 'paid',
    updated_at = now();

  -- Update Job status to quote_declined
  UPDATE public.jobs
  SET status = 'quote_declined',
      completed_at = now(),
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = p_job_id;

  INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
  VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'quote_declined', 'Quote declined after arrival. Visit charge ₹' || v_visit_charge || ' collected in cash.');

  -- Add platform commission to mechanic fee ledger
  INSERT INTO public.payments (
    invoice_id,
    method,
    amount,
    platform_fee,
    status
  )
  SELECT id, 'cash', v_visit_charge, v_platform_fee, 'completed'
  FROM public.invoices
  WHERE job_id = p_job_id;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'success', true,
    'status', 'quote_declined',
    'visit_charge', v_visit_charge,
    'platform_fee', v_platform_fee
  );
END;
$$;

-- -------------------------------------------------------------
-- 4. COMPLETE JOB CASH WITH APP_SETTINGS FEE CALCULATION RPC
-- -------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.complete_job_cash_server(
  p_job_id UUID,
  p_spare_parts_amount NUMERIC DEFAULT 0,
  p_finish_code TEXT DEFAULT NULL
)
RETURNS JSONB
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_job RECORD;
  v_quote RECORD;
  v_code RECORD;
  v_visit_charge NUMERIC := 200;
  v_platform_percent NUMERIC := 10;
  v_labor_charge NUMERIC := 0;
  v_parts_total NUMERIC := COALESCE(p_spare_parts_amount, 0);
  v_grand_total NUMERIC;
  v_platform_fee NUMERIC;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO v_job FROM public.jobs WHERE id = p_job_id;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
  END IF;

  -- 1. Verify finish code
  IF p_finish_code IS NOT NULL THEN
    SELECT * INTO v_code
    FROM public.secure_codes
    WHERE job_id = p_job_id AND code_type = 'finish' AND is_used = false;

    IF FOUND THEN
      IF TRIM(v_code.code) != TRIM(p_finish_code) THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid Finish Code provided';
      END IF;

      UPDATE public.secure_codes
      SET is_used = true, used_at = now()
      WHERE id = v_code.id;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- 2. Read quote details
  SELECT * INTO v_quote FROM public.quotes WHERE job_id = p_job_id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;
  IF FOUND THEN
    v_visit_charge := COALESCE(v_quote.visit_fee, 200);
    v_labor_charge := COALESCE(v_quote.labor_cost, 0);
  ELSE
    SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 200) INTO v_visit_charge FROM public.app_settings WHERE key = 'visit_charge_amount';
  END IF;

  -- 3. Read platform_fee_percent from app_settings
  SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 10) INTO v_platform_percent
  FROM public.app_settings
  WHERE key = 'platform_fee_percent';

  -- 4. Calculate total and platform fee server-side
  v_grand_total := v_visit_charge + v_labor_charge + v_parts_total;
  v_platform_fee := ROUND(v_grand_total * (v_platform_percent / 100.0), 2);

  -- 5. Upsert Invoice
  INSERT INTO public.invoices (
    job_id,
    quote_id,
    visit_charge,
    repair_amount,
    parts_amount,
    subtotal,
    platform_fee,
    total,
    status
  ) VALUES (
    p_job_id,
    v_quote.id,
    v_visit_charge,
    v_labor_charge,
    v_parts_total,
    v_grand_total,
    v_platform_fee,
    v_grand_total,
    'paid'
  )
  ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE SET
    visit_charge = v_visit_charge,
    repair_amount = v_labor_charge,
    parts_amount = v_parts_total,
    subtotal = v_grand_total,
    platform_fee = v_platform_fee,
    total = v_grand_total,
    status = 'paid',
    updated_at = now();

  -- 6. Update Job status to completed
  UPDATE public.jobs
  SET status = 'completed',
      completed_at = now(),
      repair_completed_at = now(),
      updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = p_job_id;

  INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
  VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'completed', 'Job marked completed. Total ₹' || v_grand_total || ' collected in cash. Commission ₹' || v_platform_fee);

  -- 7. Record cash payment and commission ledger
  INSERT INTO public.payments (
    invoice_id,
    method,
    amount,
    platform_fee,
    status
  )
  SELECT id, 'cash', v_grand_total, v_platform_fee, 'completed'
  FROM public.invoices
  WHERE job_id = p_job_id;

  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'success', true,
    'status', 'completed',
    'total', v_grand_total,
    'platform_fee', v_platform_fee,
    'mechanic_net', (v_grand_total - v_platform_fee)
  );
END;
$$;

11: -- 1. CANCEL JOB BY CUSTOMER RPC
12: -- -------------------------------------------------------------
13: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.cancel_job_by_customer(
14:   p_job_id UUID,
15:   p_reason TEXT DEFAULT 'Customer cancelled'
16: )
17: RETURNS JSONB
18: LANGUAGE plpgsql
19: SECURITY DEFINER
20: AS $$
21: DECLARE
22:   v_job RECORD;
23:   v_has_started BOOLEAN;
24: BEGIN
25:   SELECT j.*, sc.is_used as start_code_used
26:   INTO v_job
27:   FROM public.jobs j
28:   LEFT JOIN public.secure_codes sc ON sc.job_id = j.id AND sc.code_type = 'start'
29:   WHERE j.id = p_job_id;
30: 
31:   IF NOT FOUND THEN
32:     RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
33:   END IF;
34: 
35:   v_has_started := COALESCE(v_job.start_code_used, false) OR v_job.status IN ('started', 'repair_in_progress', 'quote_approved', 'bill_ready', 'completed');
36: 
37:   -- If customer cancels before mechanic arrives (start code not entered), NO fee, increment cancellation_count
38:   IF NOT v_has_started THEN
39:     UPDATE public.customers
40:     SET cancellation_count = COALESCE(cancellation_count, 0) + 1
41:     WHERE id = v_job.customer_id;
42: 
43:     UPDATE public.jobs
44:     SET status = 'cancelled',
45:         cancelled_at = now(),
46:         cancellation_reason = p_reason,
47:         updated_at = now()
48:     WHERE id = p_job_id;
49: 
50:     UPDATE public.repair_requests
51:     SET status = 'cancelled',
52:         updated_at = now()
53:     WHERE id = v_job.request_id;
54: 
55:     INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
56:     VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'cancelled', 'Customer cancelled before arrival. Reason: ' || p_reason);
57: 
58:     RETURN jsonb_build_object(
59:       'success', true,
60:       'status', 'cancelled',
61:       'fee_owed', 0,
62:       'message', 'Job cancelled without fees as mechanic had not arrived'
63:     );
64:   ELSE
65:     -- If already arrived/started, customer must decline quote or pay visit charge
66:     RAISE EXCEPTION 'Mechanic has already arrived. Please use Decline Quote flow instead of cancelling.';
67:   END IF;
68: END;
69: $$;

164:     p_job_id,
165:     v_visit_charge,
166:     0,
167:     0,
168:     v_visit_charge,
169:     v_platform_fee,
170:     v_visit_charge,
171:     'paid'
172:   )
173:   ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE SET
174:     visit_charge = v_visit_charge,
175:     repair_amount = 0,
176:     parts_amount = 0,
177:     subtotal = v_visit_charge,
178:     platform_fee = v_platform_fee,
179:     total = v_visit_charge,
180:     status = 'paid',
181:     updated_at = now();
182: 
183:   -- Update Job status to quote_declined
184:   UPDATE public.jobs
185:   SET status = 'quote_declined',
186:       completed_at = now(),
187:       updated_at = now()
188:   WHERE id = p_job_id;
189: 
190:   INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
191:   VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'quote_declined', 'Quote declined after arrival. Visit charge ₹' || v_visit_charge || ' collected in cash.');
192: 
193:   -- Add platform commission to mechanic fee ledger
194:   INSERT INTO public.payments (
195:     invoice_id,
196:     method,
197:     amount,
198:     platform_fee,
199:     status
200:   )
201:   SELECT id, 'cash', v_visit_charge, v_platform_fee, 'completed'
202:   FROM public.invoices
203:   WHERE job_id = p_job_id;
204: 
205:   RETURN jsonb_build_object(
206:     'success', true,
207:     'status', 'quote_declined',
208:     'visit_charge', v_visit_charge,
209:     'platform_fee', v_platform_fee
210:   );
211: END;
212: $$;
213: 
214: -- -------------------------------------------------------------
215: -- 4. COMPLETE JOB CASH WITH APP_SETTINGS FEE CALCULATION RPC
216: -- -------------------------------------------------------------
217: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.complete_job_cash_server(
218:   p_job_id UUID,
219:   p_spare_parts_amount NUMERIC DEFAULT 0,
220:   p_finish_code TEXT DEFAULT NULL
221: )
222: RETURNS JSONB
223: LANGUAGE plpgsql
224: SECURITY DEFINER
225: AS $$
226: DECLARE
227:   v_job RECORD;
228:   v_quote RECORD;
229:   v_code RECORD;
230:   v_visit_charge NUMERIC := 200;
231:   v_platform_percent NUMERIC := 10;
232:   v_labor_charge NUMERIC := 0;
233:   v_parts_total NUMERIC := COALESCE(p_spare_parts_amount, 0);
234:   v_grand_total NUMERIC;
235:   v_platform_fee NUMERIC;
236: BEGIN
237:   SELECT * INTO v_job FROM public.jobs WHERE id = p_job_id;
238:   IF NOT FOUND THEN
239:     RAISE EXCEPTION 'Job % not found', p_job_id;
240:   END IF;
241: 
242:   -- 1. Verify finish code
243:   IF p_finish_code IS NOT NULL THEN
244:     SELECT * INTO v_code
245:     FROM public.secure_codes
246:     WHERE job_id = p_job_id AND code_type = 'finish' AND is_used = false;
247: 
248:     IF FOUND THEN
249:       IF TRIM(v_code.code) != TRIM(p_finish_code) THEN
250:         RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid Finish Code provided';
251:       END IF;
252: 
253:       UPDATE public.secure_codes
254:       SET is_used = true, used_at = now()
255:       WHERE id = v_code.id;
256:     END IF;
257:   END IF;
258: 
259:   -- 2. Read quote details
260:   SELECT * INTO v_quote FROM public.quotes WHERE job_id = p_job_id ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1;
261:   IF FOUND THEN
262:     v_visit_charge := COALESCE(v_quote.visit_fee, 200);
263:     v_labor_charge := COALESCE(v_quote.labor_cost, 0);
264:   ELSE
265:     SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 200) INTO v_visit_charge FROM public.app_settings WHERE key = 'visit_charge_amount';
266:   END IF;
267: 
268:   -- 3. Read platform_fee_percent from app_settings
269:   SELECT COALESCE(value::numeric, 10) INTO v_platform_percent
270:   FROM public.app_settings
271:   WHERE key = 'platform_fee_percent';
272: 
273:   -- 4. Calculate total and platform fee server-side
274:   v_grand_total := v_visit_charge + v_labor_charge + v_parts_total;
275:   v_platform_fee := ROUND(v_grand_total * (v_platform_percent / 100.0), 2);
276: 
277:   -- 5. Upsert Invoice
278:   INSERT INTO public.invoices (
279:     job_id,
280:     quote_id,
281:     visit_charge,
282:     repair_amount,
283:     parts_amount,
284:     subtotal,
285:     platform_fee,
286:     total,
287:     status
288:   ) VALUES (
289:     p_job_id,
290:     v_quote.id,
291:     v_visit_charge,
292:     v_labor_charge,
293:     v_parts_total,
294:     v_grand_total,
295:     v_platform_fee,
296:     v_grand_total,
297:     'paid'
298:   )
299:   ON CONFLICT (job_id) DO UPDATE SET
300:     visit_charge = v_visit_charge,
301:     repair_amount = v_labor_charge,
302:     parts_amount = v_parts_total,
303:     subtotal = v_grand_total,
304:     platform_fee = v_platform_fee,
305:     total = v_grand_total,
306:     status = 'paid',
307:     updated_at = now();
308: 
309:   -- 6. Update Job status to completed
310:   UPDATE public.jobs
311:   SET status = 'completed',
312:       completed_at = now(),
313:       repair_completed_at = now(),
314:       updated_at = now()
315:   WHERE id = p_job_id;
316: 
317:   INSERT INTO public.job_status_history (job_id, old_status, new_status, notes)
318:   VALUES (p_job_id, v_job.status, 'completed', 'Job marked completed. Total ₹' || v_grand_total || ' collected in cash. Commission ₹' || v_platform_fee);
319: 
320:   -- 7. Record cash payment and commission ledger
321:   INSERT INTO public.payments (
322:     invoice_id,
323:     method,
324:     amount,
325:     platform_fee,
326:     status
327:   )
328:   SELECT id, 'cash', v_grand_total, v_platform_fee, 'completed'
329:   FROM public.invoices
330:   WHERE job_id = p_job_id;
331: 
332:   RETURN jsonb_build_object(
333:     'success', true,
334:     'status', 'completed',
335:     'total', v_grand_total,
336:     'platform_fee', v_platform_fee,
337:     'mechanic_net', (v_grand_total - v_platform_fee)
338:   );
339: END;
340: $$;
